info.name: VotEleven Backend
info.description:
Manual end-to-end collection generated from the current NestJS controllers, DTOs, guards, and service response shapes.

Prerequisites: run the backend and MongoDB, select the VotEleven Local environment, and start with a clean database. Run folders in numeric order. Protected folders default to User A bearer authentication; requests executed as another user override it explicitly.

Manual token limitation: development selects NoopMailService. Verification, password-reset, and invitation raw tokens are hashed in MongoDB and are not returned by the API. Requests that need them skip automatically while their environment variable is blank. Populate those values only from an authorized real/captured mail delivery.

Helper User D: the current team generator requires an even participant count. A/B/C must all participate for the requested C-to-A vote, so a fourth group member is required for a valid generated lineup.

Current HTTP blockers discovered during inspection: @UsePipes(MongoIdPipe) is attached at method level on several body-bearing Groups, Matches, and Voting routes, while MongoIdPipe validates every received value as an ObjectId. Those DTO bodies can be rejected with BAD_REQUEST before service logic. MatchStatusDto.status also lacks a class-validator decorator, so the global whitelist can reject status as a non-whitelisted property. Consequently, the current HTTP API cannot reliably reach completed status and valid voting solely through this collection. Exact intended requests remain included, with no database/token workaround invented.

item.name: 04 - Matches
item.description: Defaults to owner User A. Intended lifecycle is draft -> set an even participant list -> generate teams (ready) -> status completed. The current controller pipe/status DTO limitations described at collection level block this full lifecycle over HTTP.

request.description: Creates status draft and empty teams/participants, then captures id as matchId. Current method-level MongoIdPipe may reject this DTO body.
Owner-only partial update. Current method-level MongoIdPipe may reject this DTO body.
All IDs must be group members. Four users are used because generate-teams rejects odd participant counts. Current method-level MongoIdPipe may reject this DTO body.
Owner-only. Deterministically sorts participants, alternates home/away, and changes draft to ready.
The service only accepts ready -> completed. Current MatchStatusDto.status has no class-validator decorator, so the global whitelist can reject this body as VALIDATION_ERROR before the service runs.

item.name: 05 - Voting
item.description: All routes require group membership. Vote creation additionally requires a completed match and both voter/target in participantUserIds. Voter identity always comes from the bearer token.

item.name: 90 - Negative Tests
item.description: Run after the happy-path folders unless a request description says otherwise. Assertions use deterministic current status/error codes. Some vote business-rule scenarios are intercepted by the current method-level MongoIdPipe and therefore currently yield BAD_REQUEST before VotingService.

item.name: Non-owner User B Attempts Group Delete

request.description: Uses a bodyless owner-only route so the authorization rule is reached. The group must remain intact.
Business intent is SELF_VOTE_NOT_ALLOWED. In the current HTTP path MongoIdPipe can reject the DTO object first, producing BAD_REQUEST.

request.description: Business intent is VOTE_ALREADY_EXISTS after a successful first vote. Current method-level MongoIdPipe can intercept first with BAD_REQUEST.
Global DTO validation deterministically rejects scores outside the inclusive 1-5 range.
